bibl.title: Auditory cortex shapes sound responses in the inferior colliculus

person.p: the tag layer; a sentence written by the tagger about the paper, always anchored to a quotation but not itself a quotation

span.label: the descending feedback projection from auditory cortex to inferior colliculus, and what it does to sound responses in the structure below it
span.quote: The goal of the present study is to examine the role of cortico-collicular projections in shaping sound responses in IC.

span.label: whether selectively driving or silencing cortico-collicular projections — and separately, changing cortical inhibition — alters spontaneous and sound-evoked activity in the inferior colliculus
span.quote: In this study, we selectively modulated activity in AC, targeting either excitatory projections or inhibitory interneurons, to quantify how AC shapes spontaneous activity and sound-evoked responses in IC.

span.label: an asymmetry: activating the projection changes collicular responses, silencing it changes nothing, and interneuron-driven changes in cortex do not reach the colliculus at all
span.quote: Combined, our results identify that activation of excitatory projections, but not inhibition-driven changes in cortical activity, affects collicular sound responses.

span.label: mechanism
span.quote: Combined, our results identify that activation of excitatory projections, but not inhibition-driven changes in cortical activity, affects collicular sound responses.

span.label: cortico-collicular feedback modulation of inferior colliculus sound responses
span.quote: The goal of the present study is to examine the role of cortico-collicular projections in shaping sound responses in IC.

span.label: electrophysiology
span.quote: We measured the effects of selective optogenetic modulation of cortico-collicular feedback projections on IC sound responses in mice.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: The cortico-collicular pathway is silent or weak at rest, so it only alters collicular responses when it is actively driven, which is why suppression produces no effect while activation does.
span.quote: This result suggests that AC-IC inputs at rest do not contribute to IC responses, but rather modulate collicular activity only when activated.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: Active feedback suppresses the strongly driven responses at the receptive-field centre while boosting weakly driven responses, flattening the tuning curve and shrinking the STRF.
span.quote: cortico-collicular feedback leads to a decrease in responsiveness to tones that evoke the greatest responses (in the center of the receptive field) and an increase to stimuli that evoke weaker activity.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: Cortical inhibitory modulation does not back-propagate: changes PV interneurons impose on cortical output fail to reach the colliculus, so inhibition-driven cortical changes leave IC sound responses intact.
span.quote: Whereas modulating PVs did not have an effect on IC activity, SST suppression resulted in an increase in spontaneous, but not tone-evoked activity in IC, which suggests that inhibitory modulation of sound responses in AC does not propagate to IC.

span.label: the selectivity of the manipulation is the whole design: a retrograde virus makes only the IC-projecting cortical neurons Cre-positive, and the FLEX opsin then expresses only in those
span.quote: We used viral transfection methods to selectively drive excitatory or inhibitory opsin expression in AC-IC projections.

span.label: the reason for building it that way is stated as a defect of the earlier literature — electrical stimulation and drug inactivation cannot pick out projection neurons
span.quote: Previous studies demonstrated that activity in IC is altered by focal electrical stimulation and pharmacological inactivation of AC, but these methods lack the ability to selectively manipulate projection neurons.

span.label: the effect appears where the anatomy puts the axons: the changes are in the DCIC, which is where AC projections are densest
span.quote: This is consistent with the enhanced density of AC projections in DCIC as compared to CNIC

span.label: silence on suppression is read as a statement about the resting state — the pathway contributes nothing at baseline and only matters once driven
span.quote: This result suggests that AC-IC inputs at rest do not contribute to IC responses, but rather modulate collicular activity only when activated.

span.label: the same conclusion is reached a second way, from clicks: removing the input during cortical activity still changes nothing
span.quote: Because attenuating the input does not affect the activity in IC during clicks, this result further suggests that the strength of the baseline signal from AC to IC, even in the presence of cortical activity, is not sufficient to modulate IC responses.

span.label: an increase in firing together with a decrease in selectivity is one mechanism, not two: the suppression falls on the strongest responses
span.quote: indicate that the decrease in frequency selectivity was due to a decrease in response to tones at preferred frequencies, not non-preferred frequencies

span.label: All recordings were made in passively listening mice, so the null effect of suppressing the feedback pathway may reflect the absence of task engagement rather than the absence of a role.
span.quote: One caveat of our study is that our experiments were performed in passively listening mice.

span.label: Optogenetic activation used square laser pulses; more complex stimulation patterns might have produced stronger or different effects.
span.quote: One caveat is that we used a square pulse for optogenetic manipulations, whereas a more complex stimulation pattern potentially can achieve stronger activation ( Vila et al., 2019 ).

span.label: Cortico-collicular neurons also send collaterals to thalamus, amygdala and striatum, so the observed IC changes may partly arise through those secondary pathways rather than the direct projection.
span.quote: When interpreting our results, it is important to consider that the effects we observe from activating cortico-collicular feedback may also be due, at least in part, to these secondary pathways.

span.label: Optogenetic manipulation cannot reproduce the spatial (tonotopic) specificity of focal electrical stimulation used in earlier studies.
span.quote: Whereas optogenetic manipulation allows for temporally precise control and cell-type specificity, the technique lacks the spatial specificity of electrical stimulation.

span.label: Most recordings were multi-unit, so the reported drop in frequency selectivity could reflect firing-rate changes in differently tuned single units rather than broadened tuning per neuron.
span.quote: Because the majority of the units were recorded as multi-units, it is possible that this change in selectivity is due to the change in firing rate of differentially tuned single units.

span.label: the animals were listening passively, and the authors expect the null result for suppression to be a consequence of that
span.quote: One caveat of our study is that our experiments were performed in passively listening mice.

span.label: the manipulated neurons also project to thalamus, amygdala and striatum, so the measured effect need not have travelled by the pathway named in the title
span.quote: An important consideration with this method, however, is that these neurons do not only send collaterals to IC, but also to the auditory thalamus

span.label: optogenetics buys cell-type specificity at the cost of spatial specificity, and the pathway is tonotopic — so a whole-map activation cannot reproduce the frequency-specific shifts electrical stimulation produced
span.quote: Whereas optogenetic manipulation allows for temporally precise control and cell-type specificity, the technique lacks the spatial specificity of electrical stimulation.

span.label: most recordings are multi-unit, so a change in selectivity may be a change in the mix of differently tuned single units rather than in any neuron's tuning
span.quote: Because the majority of the units were recorded as multi-units, it is possible that this change in selectivity is due to the change in firing rate of differentially tuned single units.

span.label: a square light pulse may simply be too crude a drive to produce the full effect
span.quote: One caveat is that we used a square pulse for optogenetic manipulations, whereas a more complex stimulation pattern potentially can achieve stronger activation

span.label: retrograde Cre plus a FLEX opsin, used to make a projection — not a cell type and not a region — the unit of manipulation
span.quote: We used viral transfection methods to selectively drive excitatory or inhibitory opsin expression in AC-IC projections.

span.label: sparseness as the measure of how selective a tuning curve is
span.quote: To examine frequency selectivity of neurons, sparseness of frequency tuning was computed as:

span.label: the spectro-temporal receptive field, estimated from dynamic random chords
span.quote: The unbiased nature of this stimulus allowed us to estimate the spectro-temporal receptive field of neurons (STRF), which quantifies the dynamics of sound waveform in time and frequency that lead to a neuronal response.

span.label: slope and intercept of an on-versus-off fit, used to separate a multiplicative change in gain from an additive one
span.quote: This analysis can reveal whether changes in frequency selectivity are linear/subtractive, multiplicative/divisive, or some combination of these transformations.

span.label: the initial cohort of recordings was made under ANAESTHESIA, and awake and anaesthetised cohorts were then analysed separately before being pooled
span.quote: Initial experiments were performed under anesthesia to control for stability or recordings. For cohorts with awake and anesthetized recordings data were analyzed separately, but we observed no difference in our results so data were combined

span.label: THE TEST THAT DID NOT TEST THE CLAIM: a reviewer objects that a Kolmogorov-Smirnov test of normality cannot support a claim that the manipulation changed firing
span.quote: Instead, the authors have chosen to use a Kolmogorov-Smirnoff test to ask when the distribution of change in firing rate was normally distributed. However, it is not possible to conclude from this that the cortical activation actually has caused a significant change.

span.label: AND THE AUTHORS RE-RAN IT: the reported statistic was replaced with a paired Wilcoxon sign-rank test on the same data, and the conclusion survived
span.quote: To address this concern, we performed a paired Wilcoxon sign-rank test on the laser on vs laser off firing rate of each unit. We still observe significant increases in firing rate with ChR2 activation of AC-IC feedback.

span.label: SAMPLE SIZE DECIDED WHAT EXISTED: earlier work found no feedback effect in central IC; recording more neurons revealed a subset there
span.quote: In our study we were able to record from a larger neuronal population, revealing a subset of neurons in central IC that were modulated by feedback.

span.label: AN ASYMMETRY BETWEEN DRIVING AND SILENCING is the paper's central result, and it is read as a claim about the resting state rather than as a failed manipulation
span.quote: This result suggests that AC-IC inputs at rest do not contribute to IC responses, but rather modulate collicular activity only when activated.

span.label: MORE FIRING, LESS TUNING: the feedback is described as reducing selectivity rather than sharpening it, against the expectation the earlier stimulation literature set
span.quote: Overall our findings imply that direct cortico-collicular feedback can modulate responses to simple (pure tones) and more complex (DRCs) auditory stimuli by reducing, rather than increasing, sound selectivity.

span.label: THE SAME RESULT SAID PLAINLY, in the authors' own restatement
span.quote: In other words, neuronal firing increases overall, but selective responses to specific frequency bands decrease.

span.label: AN EFFECT SMALLER THAN EXPECTED IS REPORTED AS SUCH, and read as evidence that the target population inside IC is small
span.quote: Whereas the direction of the effect was consistent with our prior expectations, the magnitude of the effect was unexpectedly small.

span.label: A NEGATIVE RESULT ABOUT INHIBITION: changes made by PV interneurons in cortex do not reach the colliculus
span.quote: This suggests that the changes in cortical activity driven by manipulation of PV activity does not propagate to the inferior colliculus.

span.label: SST IS NOT PV: suppressing SST interneurons moves spontaneous activity in IC where PV manipulation moves nothing — a dissociation between two inhibitory subtypes
span.quote: SST suppression resulted in an increase in spontaneous, but not tone-evoked activity in IC, which suggests that inhibitory modulation of sound responses in AC does not propagate to IC

span.label: THE FIELD'S DEFAULT IS ASCENDING: descending feedback is described as routinely overlooked
span.quote: Information processing is typically studied as a set of computations ascending along a hierarchy of sensory areas, often overlooking the role of descending feedback between these nuclei.

span.label: A ROBUSTNESS CHECK AGAINST A SELECTION ARTEFACT: the DCIC result is re-run on rate-matched units in case a few high-firing units carried it
span.quote: To verify that these results were not due to a select few high firing rates of units in DCIC, we repeated the analysis comparing only units with spontaneous activity in the laser OFF condition less than 40 Hz.

span.label: TWO MECHANISMS FOR ONE OBSERVATION ARE LEFT OPEN: direct activation and disinhibition are not equivalent, which is offered as why the interneuron result differs
span.quote: Direct activation causes synchronized activation of cells, while disinhibition allows for asynchronous activation.

span.label: THE TEST THAT DID NOT TEST THE CLAIM: a reviewer objects that a Kolmogorov-Smirnov test of normality cannot support a claim that the manipulation changed firing
span.quote: Instead, the authors have chosen to use a Kolmogorov-Smirnoff test to ask when the distribution of change in firing rate was normally distributed. However, it is not possible to conclude from this that the cortical activation actually has caused a significant change.

span.label: replicates → Vila et al., 2019
span.quote: This is consistent with another study which observed enhanced white noise-induced activity in a small subset of neurons in the CNIC with activation of direct cortico-collicular feedback ( Vila et al., 2019 ).

span.label: extends → Xiong et al., 2015
span.quote: Previous studies found no effect of activating projection terminals on responses in the CNIC, only shell regions of IC ( Xiong et al., 2015 ), which are the predominant targets of cortico-collicular feedback.

span.label: builds-on → Aizenberg and Geffen, 2013; Aizenberg et al., 2015
span.quote: Previously, we found that behavioral frequency discrimination acuity changed after differential auditory fear conditioning and these changes were driven by the auditory cortex ( Aizenberg and Geffen, 2013 ; Aizenberg et al., 2015 ).

span.label: does_not_replicate → the best-frequency shift in IC reported after electrical stimulation of AC
span.quote: when activating direct feedback, we did not observe consistent changes in best frequency of IC neurons

span.label: extends → Xiong et al. 2015, which found feedback effects only in shell regions and not in central IC
span.quote: In our study we were able to record from a larger neuronal population, revealing a subset of neurons in central IC that were modulated by feedback.

span.label: agrees_with → the inactivation literature, which found no effect of AC inactivation on frequency selectivity in IC
span.quote: Previous inactivation studies have shown mixed effects on sound-evoked responses in IC, but consistently demonstrated no effect on frequency selectivity, agreeing with our results.

span.label: qualifies → the claim that cortico-collicular feedback shapes hearing, by restricting it to states in which the pathway is actively driven
span.quote: This result suggests that AC-IC inputs at rest do not contribute to IC responses, but rather modulate collicular activity only when activated.

span.label: motivated_by → the behavioural finding that this pathway is required for auditory learning
span.quote: Cortico-collicular feedback is critical to auditory learning, specifically learning to adapt to a unilateral earplug during sound localization

span.label: RETRACTED (RE-GROUNDED) · cortico-collicular feedback —causes→ spontaneous activity
span.quote: Activation of feedback increased spontaneous activity and decreased stimulus selectivity in IC, whereas suppression had no effect.

span.label: cortico-collicular feedback —causes→ frequency selectivity
span.quote: Overall our findings imply that direct cortico-collicular feedback can modulate responses to simple (pure tones) and more complex (DRCs) auditory stimuli by reducing, rather than increasing, sound selectivity.

span.label: frequency selectivity —operationalised-as→ sparseness
span.quote: To examine frequency selectivity of neurons, sparseness of frequency tuning was computed as:

span.label: tone-evoked response magnitude —part-of→ spontaneous activity
span.quote: Tone-evoked response magnitude was calculated as the difference between the average tone-evoked response in a 75 ms window after tone onset and the spontaneous activity.

span.label: DCIC —distinct-from→ CNIC
span.quote: Interestingly, these changes were observed almost exclusively in cells located in DCIC rather than CNIC

span.label: RETRACTED (RE-GROUNDED) · parvalbumin-positive interneuron —distinct-from→ somatostatin-positive interneuron
span.quote: SST suppression resulted in an increase in spontaneous, but not tone-evoked activity in IC, which suggests that inhibitory modulation of sound responses in AC does not propagate to IC

span.label: auditory cortex —causes→ inferior colliculus
span.quote: Combined, our results identify that activation of excitatory projections, but not inhibition-driven changes in cortical activity, affects collicular sound responses.

span.label: cortico-collicular feedback —is-a→ descending feedback
span.quote: Information processing is typically studied as a set of computations ascending along a hierarchy of sensory areas, often overlooking the role of descending feedback between these nuclei.

span.label: RETRACTED (RE-GROUNDED) · ChR2 —operationalised-as→ cortico-collicular feedback
span.quote: We used viral transfection methods to selectively drive excitatory or inhibitory opsin expression in AC-IC projections.

span.label: RETRACTED (RE-GROUNDED) · ArchT —operationalised-as→ cortico-collicular feedback
span.quote: We used viral transfection methods to selectively drive excitatory or inhibitory opsin expression in AC-IC projections.

span.label: RETRACTED (ENDPOINT ABSENT FROM ITS OWN EVIDENCE, AND NEITHER NAME IS THE PAPER'S) · paired Wilcoxon sign-rank test —distinct-from→ Kolmogorov-Smirnov test
span.quote: Instead, the authors have chosen to use a Kolmogorov-Smirnoff test to ask when the distribution of change in firing rate was normally distributed. However, it is not possible to conclude from this that the cortical activation actually has caused a significant change.

span.label: RETRACTED (THE `to` ENDPOINT IS NOT IN THE SPAN) · spectro-temporal receptive field —operationalised-as→ frequency selectivity
span.quote: The unbiased nature of this stimulus allowed us to estimate the spectro-temporal receptive field of neurons (STRF), which quantifies the dynamics of sound waveform in time and frequency that lead to a neuronal response.

span.label: best frequency —contrasted-with→ cortico-collicular feedback
span.quote: when activating direct feedback, we did not observe consistent changes in best frequency of IC neurons

span.label: noise correlation —contrasted-with→ cortico-collicular feedback
span.quote: We found that activating cortico-collicular feedback using ChR2 had no effect on noise correlations during spontaneous activity or tone response

span.label: cortico-collicular feedback —part-of→ layer 5
span.quote: IC receives glutamatergic ( Feliciano and Potashner, 1995 ) inputs from neurons originating predominantly in layer 5 of AC

span.label: RETRACTED (RE-GROUNDED) · dynamic random chords —operationalised-as→ spectro-temporal receptive field
span.quote: The unbiased nature of this stimulus allowed us to estimate the spectro-temporal receptive field of neurons (STRF), which quantifies the dynamics of sound waveform in time and frequency that lead to a neuronal response.

span.label: RETRACTED (THE DIRECTION IS INVERTED BY A SUPPRESSION EXPERIMENT) · somatostatin-positive interneuron —causes→ spontaneous activity
span.quote: SST suppression resulted in an increase in spontaneous, but not tone-evoked activity in IC, which suggests that inhibitory modulation of sound responses in AC does not propagate to IC

span.label: parvalbumin-positive interneuron —causes→ auditory cortex
span.quote: Specifically, in AC, activating PVs decreased spontaneous activity and tone-evoked response magnitude

span.label: RETRACTED (THE SPAN IS A REVIEWER'S TEXT, NOT THE PAPER'S) · Wilcoxon sign-rank test —distinct-from→ Kolmogorov-Smirnoff test
span.quote: Instead, the authors have chosen to use a Kolmogorov-Smirnoff test to ask when the distribution of change in firing rate was normally distributed. However, it is not possible to conclude from this that the cortical activation actually has caused a significant change. Instead, it would be appropriate to conduct a dependant-samples t-test for laser ON vs laser OFF firing rates (or indeed a Wilcoxon sign-rank test if these data are not normally distributed, as is applied elsewhere in the manuscript)

span.label: parvalbumin-positive interneuron —distinct-from→ somatostatin-positive interneuron
span.quote: In Pvalb-Cr e mice Cre recombinase (Cre) was expressed in parvalbumin-positive interneurons, and in Sst-Cre , Cre was expressed in somatostatin-positive interneurons.

span.label: ChR2 —operationalised-as→ cortico-collicular feedback
span.quote: We found that activating cortico-collicular feedback using ChR2 increased spontaneous activity of IC neurons

span.label: ArchT —operationalised-as→ cortico-collicular feedback
span.quote: By contrast, suppressing cortico-collicular feedback using ArchT had no effect on IC click responses

span.label: cortico-collicular feedback —causes→ spontaneous activity
span.quote: We found that activating cortico-collicular feedback using ChR2 increased spontaneous activity of IC neurons ( Figure 3A , left; −100 ms: p=0.022, ON = 4.3 ± 0.47 Hz; OFF = 3.6 ± 0.38; −20 ms: p=8.6e-6, ON = 5.6 ± 0.63, OFF = 3.7 ± 0.47).

span.label: dynamic random chords —operationalised-as→ spectro-temporal receptive field
span.quote: To better understand the effect of modulation of cortical activity on spectro-temporal receptive field properties of IC neurons, we presented a continuous signal comprised of dynamic random chords (DRCs) sampled from a uniform distribution of loudness values per frequency bin.

span.label: Wilcoxon signed-rank test
span.quote: Significant differences and P values were calculated using paired Wilcoxon sign-rank test (unless noted otherwise) with standard MATLAB routine.

span.label: Kolmogorov-Smirnov test
span.quote: For the laser alone data, to compare distributions to standard normal distribution data were normalized by mean and standard deviation and then significant differences and P values were calculated by Kolmogorov-Smirnoff test with standard MATLAB routine.

span.label: linear regression
span.quote: Linear fits were calculated using linear regression (fitlm.m; MATLAB) over 50 data points, one for each of the 50 frequencies tested

span.label: correlation
span.quote: Noise correlations were calculated as the pairwise Pearson correlation coefficient between the spike counts of units recorded simultaneously.

span.label: standard error of the mean
span.quote: standard error of the mean was reported unless stated otherwise.

span.label: z-score
span.quote: To determine the significance of the lobes, the z -score of pixels was computed relative to the baseline values from an STRF generated with scrambled spike trains, using Stat4ci toolbox

span.label: p-value
span.quote: * indicates p<0.05, ** indicates p<0.01, *** indicates p<0.001.

span.label: power analysis / effect size
span.quote: We used power analysis for effect size of 25% and expected variance in firing rate (50%) to determine the minimum total number of units for each experimental group at N

span.label: permutation/randomization test
span.quote: We ran this significance test 100 times and any pixel identified as significant more than 90 times was considered significant.

span.label: paired Wilcoxon sign-rank throughout, with a Kolmogorov-Smirnov test used only for comparing distributions to normal
span.quote: Significant differences and P values were calculated using paired Wilcoxon sign-rank test (unless noted otherwise) with standard MATLAB routine.

span.label: the reported test was changed during peer review after a reviewer objected that the original one did not address the claim
span.quote: To address this concern, we performed a paired Wilcoxon sign-rank test on the laser on vs laser off firing rate of each unit. We still observe significant increases in firing rate with ChR2 activation of AC-IC feedback.

span.label: Optogenetically activating cortico-collicular feedback raised spontaneous firing and lowered stimulus selectivity in the inferior colliculus, while suppressing the same projection changed nothing.
span.quote: Activation of feedback increased spontaneous activity and decreased stimulus selectivity in IC, whereas suppression had no effect.

span.label: Driving or silencing PV or SST inhibitory interneurons in auditory cortex left sound-evoked activity in the inferior colliculus unchanged.
span.quote: We found that modulating the activity of either type of interneuron did not affect IC sound-evoked activity.

span.label: The feedback effects appeared almost only in the dorsal cortex of the inferior colliculus, where cortical projections are densest, not in the central nucleus.
span.quote: This effect was localized to DCIC, corresponding to the sites with largest density of AC projections

span.label: The loss of frequency selectivity came from weaker responses at each unit's preferred frequencies rather than stronger responses at non-preferred ones.
span.quote: the decrease in frequency selectivity was due to a decrease in response to tones at preferred frequencies, not non-preferred frequencies.

span.label: Feedback activation raised overall firing while shrinking the frequency-specific structure of the receptive field.
span.quote: In other words, neuronal firing increases overall, but selective responses to specific frequency bands decrease.

span.label: Activating the feedback did not change trial-to-trial noise correlations between simultaneously recorded IC units.
span.quote: had no effect on noise correlations during spontaneous activity or tone response

span.label: Suppressing cortico-collicular feedback left click-evoked responses in IC untouched, indicating the pathway is not tonically shaping IC responses in passively listening mice.
span.quote: By contrast, suppressing cortico-collicular feedback using ArchT had no effect on IC click responses

span.label: The overall conclusion is that direct cortico-collicular feedback reduces rather than sharpens sound selectivity, for both simple tones and complex dynamic chords.
span.quote: Overall our findings imply that direct cortico-collicular feedback can modulate responses to simple (pure tones) and more complex (DRCs) auditory stimuli by reducing, rather than increasing, sound selectivity.

span.label: activation of the feedback raises spontaneous activity and lowers stimulus selectivity in IC; suppression does neither
span.quote: Activation of feedback increased spontaneous activity and decreased stimulus selectivity in IC, whereas suppression had no effect.

span.label: changes in cortical activity produced through PV or SST interneurons do not reach the colliculus
span.quote: Combined, our results identify that activation of excitatory projections, but not inhibition-driven changes in cortical activity, affects collicular sound responses.

span.label: the effects are confined to DCIC, the part of IC where cortical axons are densest
span.quote: Interestingly, these changes were observed almost exclusively in cells located in DCIC rather than CNIC

span.label: no consistent change in best frequency — the quantity electrical stimulation had been reported to shift
span.quote: when activating direct feedback, we did not observe consistent changes in best frequency of IC neurons

span.label: best frequency
span.quote: Best frequency was defined as the frequency that elicited the maximum response.

span.label: sparseness (measure of frequency selectivity)
span.quote: To examine frequency selectivity of neurons, sparseness of frequency tuning was computed as:

span.label: tone-evoked response magnitude
span.quote: Tone-evoked response magnitude was calculated as the difference between the average tone-evoked response in a 75 ms window after tone onset and the spontaneous activity.

span.label: noise correlations
span.quote: Noise correlations were calculated as the pairwise Pearson correlation coefficient between the spike counts of units recorded simultaneously.

span.label: spectro-temporal receptive field (STRF)
span.quote: The unbiased nature of this stimulus allowed us to estimate the spectro-temporal receptive field of neurons (STRF), which quantifies the dynamics of sound waveform in time and frequency that lead to a neuronal response.

span.label: tone-evoked response magnitude is defined by subtraction, as evoked minus spontaneous in a 75 ms window
span.quote: Tone-evoked response magnitude was calculated as the difference between the average tone-evoked response in a 75 ms window after tone onset and the spontaneous activity.

span.label: frequency selectivity is defined operationally as sparseness of frequency tuning
span.quote: To examine frequency selectivity of neurons, sparseness of frequency tuning was computed as:

span.label: optogenetic activation (ChR2) versus suppression (ArchT) of cortico-collicular projections
span.term: optogenetic activation (ChR2) versus suppression (ArchT) of cortico-collicular projections
span.quote: We measured the effects of selective optogenetic modulation of cortico-collicular feedback projections on IC sound responses in mice.

span.label: laser pulse duration
span.quote: varied the duration of laser manipulation (1 ms, 5 ms, 25 ms, 250 ms).

span.label: laser onset time relative to tone onset
span.term: laser onset time relative to tone onset
span.quote: To modulate the feedback from AC, we tested three different laser onsets (−100 ms, −20 ms, +8 ms) relative to tone onset to isolate the effect of timing on affecting IC responses.

span.label: cortical inhibitory interneuron subtype manipulated (PV vs SST)
span.term: cortical inhibitory interneuron subtype manipulated (PV vs SST)
span.quote: we perturbed the excitatory-inhibitory interactions by modulating two different classes of inhibitory interneuron known to contribute to sound responses in AC: PV and SST inhibitory interneurons

span.label: spontaneous firing rate of IC units
span.term: spontaneous firing rate of IC units
span.quote: Feedback cohort: Spontaneous activity was the average firing rate in a 20 ms window (to allow for equivalent comparison between −100 ms and −20 ms laser onset conditions) prior to tone onset of top 7 preferred frequencies.

span.label: tone-evoked response magnitude
span.quote: Tone-evoked response magnitude was calculated as the difference between the average tone-evoked response in a 75 ms window after tone onset and the spontaneous activity.

span.label: frequency selectivity measured as sparseness
span.quote: To examine frequency selectivity of neurons, sparseness of frequency tuning was computed as:

span.label: noise correlations between simultaneously recorded units
span.term: noise correlations between simultaneously recorded units
span.quote: To test whether activation of cortico-collicular feedback affected correlations in trial-to-trial variability of response strength between units recorded simultaneously we measured noise correlations.

span.label: IC recording subregion (dorsal cortex vs central nucleus)
span.term: IC recording subregion (dorsal cortex vs central nucleus)
span.quote: Recording sites in IC were identified based on anatomical markers and stereotaxic coordinates as dorsal cortex (<0.5 mm of midline) or central nucleus of IC (center of central nucleus of IC ~1 mm lateral of midline).

span.label: unit inclusion criterion based on tone responsiveness in the no-laser condition
span.term: unit inclusion criterion based on tone responsiveness in the no-laser condition
span.quote: Units with tone-evoked activity (75 ms window after tone onset) less than two standard deviations above the spontaneous activity (50 ms window prior to tone onset) in no laser condition were excluded from the analysis.

span.label: laser onset relative to tone onset is varied deliberately (−100, −20, +8 ms) to separate a steady-state effect from one timed to the cortical response
span.quote: we tested three different laser onsets (−100 ms, −20 ms, +8 ms) relative to tone onset to isolate the effect of timing on affecting IC responses

span.label: 42% — proportion of positive STRF lobes that survived feedback activation in units whose firing rate increased (63% for negative lobes)
span.quote: only 42% of positive lobes, and 63% of negative lobes persisted with the laser

span.label: <0.04% — size of the change in sparseness produced by suppressing the feedback, i.e. effectively no change in frequency selectivity
span.quote: Suppressing feedback resulted in very small (<0.04%) change in sparseness, therefore it did not affect frequency selectivity

span.label: p=0.00098 — significance of the reduction in temporal width of positive STRF lobes when feedback was activated
span.quote: Of those lobes that persisted, for positive lobes, there was on average a decrease in temporal width (p=0.00098, ON

span.label: 25% — effect size assumed in the a priori power analysis used to fix the minimum number of units per experimental group
span.quote: We used power analysis for effect size of 25% and expected variance in firing rate (50%) to determine the minimum total number of units for each experimental group at N

span.label: 3 mW — laser power delivered through the implanted cannulas for optogenetic manipulation
span.quote: Laser power measured through cannulas was 3 mW.
